questions.q: Which library is the current, supported way to connect to real IBM Quantum hardware backends?
options: qiskit-ibmq-provider
qiskit-ibm-runtime
qiskit_aer
qiskit.BasicAer
questions.explain: qiskit-ibm-runtime, via QiskitRuntimeService, is the current supported library for authenticating and interacting with IBM Quantum hardware; the older qiskit-ibmq-provider has been superseded.

options: The backend with the most total qubits
A random operational backend
The operational, non-simulator real backend with the shortest current queue
Every backend sorted by name
questions.explain: least_busy filters to backends that are online and real hardware (not cloud simulators), then returns whichever of those currently has the fewest pending jobs.

questions.q: A circuit applies a two-qubit gate between two physical qubits that are NOT adjacent on the backend's coupling map. What happens during transpilation?
options: The job is rejected outright
The gate is silently dropped from the circuit
Extra SWAP gates are inserted to move the relevant qubit states into adjacent positions first
The backend automatically adds more physical qubits
questions.explain: When a two-qubit gate targets non-adjacent physical qubits, the transpiler must insert SWAP gates to route the states together before the native two-qubit gate can be applied, which adds to the final gate count.

questions.q: Why does this lesson avoid naming a specific current IBM backend and its exact qubit count as a fixed fact?
options: Because IBM hardware details are secret
Because device availability, names, and qubit counts change over time, so a snapshot would go stale
Because qubit counts are not a real property of a backend
Because simulators are always used instead of real hardware
questions.explain: IBM retires and introduces devices and adjusts access over time, so any specific device name or qubit count quoted today could be inaccurate later — the dashboard is the authoritative current source.

questions.q: Besides qubit count, which of the following is a real factor in choosing a backend for a specific circuit?
options: The color scheme of the IBM dashboard
The backend's coupling map matching your circuit's entangling structure, and its current queue length
The number of previous users who have run jobs on it, ever
Whether the backend has ever appeared in a tutorial
questions.explain: Connectivity (coupling map) and current queue length (pending_jobs) are both real, practical criteria — a mismatched coupling map inflates gate count via routing, and a long queue delays results regardless of circuit quality.
